collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and another adult; in the story (name1) can't tell some colors apart)

collection.description: A villager who cannot tell red from some greens has dyed the new cloth green and green: laugh along, or fix it together.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) dyed the new cloth for the meeting hut today. It was supposed to be red and green stripes, like always. It has come out green and green stripes, two slightly different greens. (subject) can't see the difference between red and some greens, and has never been able to. (subject.He/she) hadn't realized until (friend) walked in and burst out laughing.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) looks at the cloth, then at (friend)'s face, and starts laughing too. "Is it bad?" "It's very green," says (friend). They hang it anyway. People come and look. A surprising number of them like it. After that, (friend) helps (subject) mark the dye pots with knots: one for red, two for green. The next cloth comes out right. Some people miss the green one.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) is embarrassed. (friend) stops laughing and helps (subject.him/her) re-dye half the stripes. While they work, (subject) explains what colors look like to (subject.him/her). (friend) is fascinated. "So the sunset is..." "Mostly yellow. Very nice yellow." The finished cloth is red and green. (friend) thinks about the yellow sunset for days.
